checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is deposit data extraction deterministic across all EL implementations?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all EL implementation codebases (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon, Reth) and locate their extract_deposit_data equivalent functions. 2. Generate a corpus of test vectors including: (a) valid 576-byte deposit log data with all field combinations, (b) edge cases for pubkey, withdrawal_credentials, amount, signature, and index field values, (c) boundary values for each ABI-encoded offset and size field. 3. Execute each test vector against all EL implementations and compare the output bytes byte-for-byte. 4. Specifically test: (a) byte ordering (big-endian vs little-endian interpretation), (b) slice boundary calculations for each of the 5 data fields, (c) concatenation order of extracted fields (pubkey||withdrawal_credentials||amount||signature||index). 5. Verify that any difference in output bytes between implementations is flagged as a consensus-critical bug. 6. Check for implementation-specific quirks in integer parsing (Python arbitrary precision vs Go/Rust fixed-width) that could produce different extraction results.
checklist.falsification_approach: Attempt to find or craft deposit log data that produces different output bytes when processed by two different EL implementations. Focus on: (1) ABI-encoded data with unusual but valid offset/size combinations, (2) Data that exercises integer boundary conditions in fixed-width implementations, (3) Log data that could be interpreted differently due to endianness assumptions.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0049, Trust Boundary: tb-002. This property is critical because any divergence in deposit data extraction will propagate to different requests hashes, causing a network split between EL clients. The invariant explicitly requires: forall (log_data, el1, el2): el1.extract_deposit_data(log_data) == el2.extract_deposit_data(log_data).

checklist.title: Verify byte-level consistency of deposit data field extraction across implementations
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Create a reference implementation test harness that extracts each individual field (pubkey: 48 bytes, withdrawal_credentials: 32 bytes, amount: 8 bytes, signature: 96 bytes, index: 8 bytes) from deposit log data. 2. For each field extraction, verify: (a) correct start offset from ABI-decoded position, (b) correct length (48/32/8/96/8 bytes respectively), (c) no off-by-one errors in slice boundaries. 3. Verify the final concatenation produces exactly 192 bytes: 48+32+8+96+8=192. 4. Test with intentionally malformed data to ensure all implementations reject the same invalid inputs consistently. 5. Perform differential fuzzing between at least two EL implementations using a shared corpus of deposit log data.
checklist.falsification_approach: Design tests that attempt to violate the invariant by finding inputs where extract_deposit_data produces different output bytes across implementations. Specific vectors: (1) Deposit data where field boundaries could be ambiguously interpreted, (2) Data that tests padding behavior differences, (3) Edge cases in ABI decoding where implementations might diverge.
checklist.notes: Supporting check for PROP-0049. Focuses on the internal logic correctness of field extraction to support the boundary security property.
